recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-13201; any future change to abatement and clinicalStatus semantics should be handled as a new Patient Care decision.
issue_request: FHIR-13201 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It requested correction of the Condition con-4 XPath so that an absent abatement element would not prohibit clinicalStatus values such as resolved; the approved resolution removed abatementBoolean, required inactive/resolved/remission only when abatement is populated, and allowed any clinicalStatus when abatement is absent.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by bac396f21d6dc845c746e29a9fb7c79e27ee6ff5, which updated the Condition spreadsheet invariant, removed abatementBoolean and the abatement-boolean search parameter, and adjusted the f204 renal example. That spreadsheet content was later migrated into the current StructureDefinition source.
additional_context: FHIR-22973 later asked to allow abated conditions with clinicalStatus not valued, but comments on that issue state FHIR-29409 made clinicalStatus 1..1 and largely made the exception irrelevant. The 2022 ElementDefinition cleanup removed XPath rows, and FHIR-39630 later reused the con-4 key for the unrelated bodyStructure/bodySite invariant; the abatement invariant is now con-3.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Condition is active in source/fhir.ini, current source/condition/structuredefinition-Condition.xml has no XPath invariant and no abatementBoolean datatype, and con-3 uses abatement.exists() implies an inactive/resolved/remission clinicalStatus coding, which matches the approved behavior.

related_jiras.note: Created the original Condition abatement/clinicalStatus invariant that FHIR-13201 corrected.
Asked to allow abated conditions with clinicalStatus not valued; comments say FHIR-29409 made that exception irrelevant.
Made Condition.clinicalStatus required and reshaped nearby invariants, preserving the abatement rule without a not-valued branch.
Later Not Persuasive report concluded the R4 abatement invariant was correct and a reported failure was likely tooling-specific.
Added the current bodyStructure/bodySite con-4 invariant, explaining why the old abatement rule is now con-3.
